title: One Kit, Four Styles
description: Hear how rock, hip-hop, jazz and electronic music each lean on different parts of the kit.

steps.title: Same drums, different feel
steps.description: You can usually tell what style a song is within a couple of seconds, and a lot of that comes from the drums. The kit is basically the same. What changes is which sounds take the lead and how they're combined. We'll go through four styles and hit a typical combination for each.

steps.title: Rock
steps.description: Rock is built on kick, snare and hi-hat. The kick drives on 1 and 3, the snare hits hard on 2 and 4, and the hi-hat keeps a steady tick over the top. Crashes mark the change from verse to chorus.

steps.title: Rock: kick and hat
steps.description: Hit the kick and closed hi-hat together. That's how beat 1 sounds in a rock groove.
steps.hint: KCK is top left, and CHH is two pads along the same row.

steps.title: Hip-hop
steps.description: Hip-hop is all about the kick and the snare or clap. People call it "boom bap": the boom is a heavy kick, the bap is the crack on 2 and 4. Beats tend to leave more space than rock, and an open hi-hat here and there adds some bounce.

steps.title: Hip-hop: kick, clap and open hat
steps.description: Hit the kick, clap and open hi-hat together. In a real beat these would be spread out more, but stacking them lets you hear the hip-hop palette in one go.
steps.hint: KCK and OHH are at either end of the top row, and CLP is bottom left.

steps.title: Jazz
steps.description: In jazz the ride cymbal keeps time, with a swinging "ding, ding-a ding" pattern. The kick is played so softly you can barely hear it (drummers call this feathering), and the snare drops in little comments instead of a hard backbeat. It's lighter and looser than rock.

steps.title: Jazz: kick and ride
steps.description: Hit the kick and ride together. Picture the kick as a soft pulse underneath and the ride doing most of the talking.
steps.hint: KCK is top left and RDE is bottom right, corner to corner.

steps.title: Electronic
steps.description: A lot of dance music runs on "four on the floor": a kick on every beat, a clap on 2 and 4, and hi-hats ticking in between, often opening up on the "and" of each beat. Crashes and cymbal swells come in during the builds.

steps.title: Electronic: kick, clap and hat
steps.description: Hit the kick, clap and closed hi-hat together. That's beat 2 or 4 of a typical dance groove, where all three land at once.
steps.hint: Kick and closed hi-hat are on the top row, and the clap is bottom left.
